AL.lo: Occupational (wage) license taxes in some cities/counties, e.g. Birmingham 1%, Bessemer 1%, Gadsden 2%; most localities have none.
AL.no: Federal income tax paid is deductible on the Alabama return. No 2025 rate change. Maximum amounts. Phase down for AGI above $25,999: single by $25 per $500 of AGI to a $2,500 floor; MFJ by $175 per $500 to a $5,000 floor. Dependent exemption $1,000 if AGI <= $50,000; $500 if $50,001-$100,000; $300 above $100,000.

AZ.no: Flat 2.5%, unchanged in 2025. HB 4168 (signed June 13, 2026) moved IRC conformity to Jan 1, 2026, with subtractions for the federal tips/overtime deductions from tax year 2025. Tied to the federal standard deduction; ADOR's Feb 2026 update gives $15,750/$31,500 for 2025 (Tax Foundation's table showed the pre-OBBBA $15,000/$30,000). Non-itemizers can add 33% of charitable contributions. No personal exemption. Dependent credit $100 per dependent under 17 and $25 per dependent 17+; phases out above FAGI $200,000 single / $400,000 MFJ.

AR.no: Brackets are DFA's 2025 regular table for net income up to $94,700 (same for all filing statuses). Above $94,700 a bracket adjustment removes the lower brackets: from $97,801, tax = 3.9% x net income - $89.30 (about 2% on the first $4,700 and 3.9% above). Separate low-income tables give lower tax at low incomes. Top rate 3.9% since 2024, unchanged in 2025. 2025 DFA instructions (Tax Foundation listed $2,410/$4,820). $29 personal tax credit per taxpayer, spouse and dependent.

CA.no: 2025 FTB brackets (Tax Foundation showed 2024). The rows at $1,000,000 add the 1% Behavioral Health Services Tax on taxable income over $1M (all filing statuses). The CA SDI payroll tax (no wage cap) is withheld separately and not included. 2025 FTB indexed amounts (Tax Foundation showed 2024 amounts). Exemption credits are cut by $6 per credit for each $2,500 of federal AGI above $252,203 (single) / $504,411 (MFJ).

CO.lo: Occupational privilege taxes (flat monthly amounts on employees working in the city): Denver $5.75/mo, Aurora $2/mo, Greenwood Village $2/mo, Sheridan $3/mo, Glendale $5/mo.
CO.no: Rate is back to 4.4% for 2025; the TABOR-triggered 4.25% applied to 2024 only. Federal standard deduction, already included because Colorado starts from federal taxable income (federal 2025: $15,750/$31,500); do not subtract again. If AGI is over $300,000, std/itemized deductions above $12,000 (single) / $16,000 (MFJ) are added back.

CT.no: Phase-outs: income in the 2% bracket is taxed at 4.5% once CT AGI exceeds $56,500 (single) / $100,500 (MFJ). Benefit recapture adds up to $3,150 (single) / $6,300 (MFJ) above $105,000 / $210,000, so very high earners pay about 6.99% on all income. No 2025 rate change. No standard deduction. Personal exemption shrinks by $1,000 for each $1,000 of CT AGI above $30,000 (single) / $48,000 (MFJ), reaching zero at $45,000 / $72,000. Personal tax credits of 1%-75% of tax also apply at lower incomes.

DE.lo: Wilmington 1.25% earned income (wage) tax on residents and on nonresidents working in the city.
DE.no: No 2025 rate change. $110 personal credit per taxpayer, spouse and dependent.

GA.no: HB 111 (April 2025) cut the rate from 5.39% to 5.19%, retroactive to Jan 1, 2025. The Tax Foundation table still shows 5.39%. No personal exemption since 2024; $4,000 per dependent.

HI.no: Act 46 (2024) widened the brackets from 2025, with more bracket and std deduction steps scheduled for later years. Doubled for 2025 under Act 46 (2024).

ID.no: HB 40 (March 2025) cut the rate from 5.695% to 5.3%, retroactive to Jan 1, 2025. The zero-rate band is indexed: $4,811 single / $9,622 MFJ (Tax Foundation shows the 2024 values $4,673/$9,346 at 5.695%). Equal to the federal amount. Idaho adopted the 2025 federal (OBBBA) changes, including the tips, overtime, car-loan-interest and senior deductions. No personal exemptions. Idaho has a separate child tax credit.

IL.no: No 2025 rate change. No standard deduction. Not allowed if AGI exceeds $250,000 (single) / $500,000 (MFJ).

IN.lo: County income tax on all residents, about 0.5%-3.0% in 2025 (e.g. Marion County/Indianapolis 2.02%).
IN.no: Rate cut from 3.05% to 3.0% for 2025. The IT-40 starting point follows the IRC as in effect on Jan 1, 2023. No standard deduction. Each qualifying dependent child gets another $1,500 ($3,000 in the first year a child is claimed).

IA.lo: School district income surtaxes, levied as a percentage of the Iowa income tax and set by each district.
IA.no: Graduated rates were replaced by a flat 3.8% for 2025. Federal standard deduction, already included because Iowa starts from federal taxable income with rolling IRC conformity (federal 2025: $15,750/$31,500); do not subtract again. $40 exemption credit per taxpayer, spouse and dependent.

KS.no: Rates unchanged for 2025: the SB 269 revenue-triggered cut was not triggered (KDOR Notice 25-06).

KY.lo: Occupational license taxes on wages in most cities/counties, typically about 0.5%-2.5% combined (e.g. Louisville Metro about 2.2% for residents, Lexington-Fayette 2.25%), plus some school district taxes.
KY.no: Rate cut from 4.5% to 4.0% for 2025. $3,270 per person. A married-filing-joint return gets only one $3,270. Couples who file 'married filing separately on a combined return' get $3,270 each ($6,540), which most two-earner couples choose. No personal exemptions. Family Size Tax Credit for low incomes; personal tax credits for 65+/blind via Schedule ITC.

LA.no: Graduated 1.85%/3.5%/4.25% replaced by a flat 3% for 2025. The old combined personal exemption-standard deduction was replaced by the std deduction above. New for 2025; indexed from 2026. Act 11 (2024 3rd Extraordinary Session) repealed the extra $1,000 deductions for dependents, age 65+ and blind.

ME.no: Brackets indexed (2025 MRS rate schedules). Maine did not adopt the federal OBBBA increase for 2025. The std/itemized deduction phases out above Maine AGI of $100,000 (single) / $200,050 (MFJ). Personal exemption of $5,150 per person (a deduction) phases out above $333,450 (single) / $400,100 (MFJ). The dependent amount is a CREDIT: $305 per dependent, $610 per child under 6, phasing out at high incomes.

MD.lo: County/Baltimore City income tax on residents, 2.25% (Worcester) to 3.30% (Dorchester) in 2025; most counties 3.2%; Anne Arundel and Frederick use graduated local rates. Nonresidents pay a 2.25% special nonresident tax instead.
MD.no: The 2025 Budget Reconciliation and Financing Act (effective tax year 2025) added 6.25% and 6.5% brackets, a flat std deduction, a 2% surtax on net capital gains when FAGI exceeds $350,000, and a 3.3% local rate cap. The Tax Foundation table predates these changes. Flat amounts from 2025, replacing the old 15%-of-income standard deduction with a minimum and maximum. $3,200 per exemption, reduced to $1,600 and then $800 as FAGI rises. It is $0 above $150,000 (single) / $200,000 (MFJ); the phase-out starts at $100,000 / $150,000.

MA.no: Effectively a flat 5%, plus a 4% surtax (9% total) on income above $1,083,150 (the same threshold for joint filers). Short-term capital gains are taxed at 8.5%. Paid Family and Medical Leave payroll contributions are separate. No standard deduction.

MI.lo: City income tax in 24 cities: most 1% for residents / 0.5% for nonresidents; Detroit 2.4% / 1.2%; Grand Rapids 1.5% / 0.75%.
MI.no: 4.25% for 2025 (the 4.05% rate applied to 2023 only). No standard deduction.

MN.no: 1% surtax on net investment income over $1 million. Reduced for high-AGI filers (above roughly $239,000, by up to 80%). No personal exemption; $5,200 per dependent.

MS.no: Rate cut from 4.7% to 4.4% for 2025, on taxable income over $10,000; 4.0% is scheduled for 2026. Another $1,500 each for 65+ or blind.

MO.lo: 1% earnings tax in Kansas City and St. Louis on residents and on nonresidents working there.
MO.no: Top rate cut from 4.8% to 4.7% for 2025. A 100% capital gains subtraction starts in 2025. A limited, AGI-phased deduction for federal income tax paid is allowed. Equals the federal std deduction (2025 OBBBA amounts per MO DOR). Missouri does NOT allow the federal tips, overtime, car-loan-interest or senior deductions.

MT.no: The start is federal taxable income computed without the QBI deduction. Net long-term capital gains are taxed at 3.0%/4.1%. HB 337 rate changes begin in 2026. Federal std deduction (and Schedule 1-A deductions), already included because Montana taxable income begins with federal AGI less federal deductions; do not subtract again. No personal exemptions (a $5,660 subtraction exists for taxpayers 65+).

NE.no: Top rate cut from 5.84% to 5.2% for 2025. $171 credit per exemption.

NH.no: Wages were never taxed. The Interest and Dividends Tax (3% in 2024) was repealed from Jan 1, 2025, so there is no individual income tax for 2025. Source: Tax Foundation; the NH DRA site refused the request (HTTP 403).

NJ.lo: None on individuals (Newark's 1% payroll tax is paid by employers).
NJ.no: No 2025 rate change. No standard deduction.

NM.no: HB 252 (2024) restructured the brackets for tax years from 2025; the top rate stays 5.9%. Equals the federal std deduction (IRC 63), so the 2025 OBBBA amounts apply. The federal tips, overtime and senior deductions do not flow through. $4,000 deduction for each dependent except one.

NY.lo: New York City resident tax 3.078%-3.876%. Yonkers: residents pay a surcharge of 16.75% of net NYS tax; nonresidents pay 0.5% of wages earned there. MCTMT applies to self-employment income in the MTA region.
NY.no: Tax benefit recapture: above NY AGI of $107,650 the benefit of the lower brackets is recaptured, so very high earners pay their top rate on all income. No 2025 rate change; cuts start in 2026. No personal exemption; $1,000 per dependent.

NC.no: Rate cut from 4.5% to 4.25% for 2025; 3.99% from 2026. No personal exemption. Child deduction per qualifying child by AGI: MFJ $3,000 up to $40,000, then $500 less per $20,000, $0 above $140,000. Single: $3,000 up to $20,000, then $500 less per $10,000, $0 above $70,000.

ND.no: 2025 brackets confirmed in ND's 2025 tax rate schedules. Federal std deduction, already included because North Dakota starts from federal taxable income; do not subtract again. Flow-through of the 2025 OBBBA amount assumes ND's automatic IRC conformity and was not separately confirmed with the state.

OH.lo: Municipal income taxes on wages in most cities, commonly 1%-2.5% (Columbus and Cleveland 2.5%, Cincinnati 1.8%), plus school district income taxes in many districts.
OH.no: HB 96 cut the top rate from 3.5% to 3.125% for 2025 (flat 2.75% from 2026); the Tax Foundation table shows 3.5%. The official table includes a base amount: income over $26,050 pays $342 + 2.75% of the excess, and income over $100,000 pays $2,394.32 + 3.125% of the excess. So the 0% band is lost above $26,050 and the marginal brackets alone understate tax by about $342. The joint filing credit and low-income credits are not modeled. No standard deduction. Per exemption by Ohio MAGI: $2,400 up to $40,000; $2,150 for $40,001-$80,000; $1,900 for $80,001-$749,999; $0 at $750,000 or more.

OK.no: No 2025 change. HB 2764 cuts the top rate to 4.5% and consolidates brackets from 2026.

OR.lo: Portland Metro Supportive Housing Services tax: 1% of taxable income above $125,000 (single) / $200,000 (joint). Multnomah County Preschool for All: 1.5% above the same thresholds, plus another 1.5% above $250,000 / $400,000.
OR.no: A subtraction for federal income tax paid (max $8,500) phases out starting at AGI $125,000 (single) / $250,000 (joint). The top bracket thresholds are not indexed. The first-bracket edges ($4,400/$8,800) are derived from DOR's published 2025 chart bases. The statewide transit tax (0.1% of wages) is withheld separately. Final 2025 DOR amounts (Tax Foundation and the 2025 estimated-tax booklet showed $2,800/$5,600). $256 credit per exemption; not allowed if federal AGI exceeds $100,000 (single) / $200,000 (joint).

PA.lo: Local earned income tax (EIT) nearly statewide, typically about 1%-2% combined municipal + school district; Pittsburgh residents 3%. Philadelphia wage tax: residents 3.75% / nonresidents 3.44% until June 30, 2025, then 3.74% / 3.43% from July 1, 2025. Many municipalities also levy a Local Services Tax (up to $52/yr).
PA.no: Income is taxed in eight state-defined classes, not from federal AGI. No 2025 rate change. No standard deduction. No personal exemptions; a Tax Forgiveness credit applies at low incomes.

RI.no: Brackets are the same for all filing statuses (indexed; 2025 values). Phases out for modified federal AGI between $254,250 and $283,250 (none above). Same $254,250-$283,250 phase-out as the std deduction.

SC.no: Top rate cut from 6.2% to 6.0% for 2025; for taxable income of $100,000 or more, tax = 6% x TI - $642. 44% of net capital gains is deductible. A major reform starts in 2026. Federal std deduction, embedded because SC starts from federal taxable income. SC conforms to the IRC as of Dec 31, 2024, so the OBBBA increase ($750 single / $1,500 MFJ) and the federal tips/overtime/senior/car-loan deductions must be added back for 2025 (SCDOR IL 26-4). No personal exemption. $4,930 per dependent, plus another $4,930 for each dependent under age 6.

TN.no: No individual income tax; the Hall tax on interest and dividends was fully repealed from 2021.

UT.no: HB 106 (2025) cut the rate from 4.55% to 4.5%, retroactive to Jan 1, 2025 (the Tax Foundation table shows 4.55%). Not a deduction. The taxpayer tax credit is 6% of the federal std deduction ($15,750/$31,500 for 2025) or of federal itemized deductions excluding state income tax. The whole credit (including the dependent part) is reduced by 1.3% of income above $18,213 (single) / $36,426 (MFJ). The Utah personal exemption is $2,111 per dependent (none for taxpayer/spouse) and enters the same 6% taxpayer credit: 6% x $2,111 = $126.66 per dependent, before the phase-out.

VT.no: Uses the 2025 VT rate schedules (Tax Foundation showed 2024 brackets). Minimum tax: if federal AGI exceeds $150,000, tax is the greater of the regular tax or 3% of AGI (less US obligation interest). Plus $1,250 for each 65+/blind box. 2025 amounts (Tax Foundation showed 2024).

VA.no: Brackets are not indexed and are the same for all filing statuses. Raised for 2025 from $8,500/$17,000. Must be used if the federal std deduction was claimed. Another $800 each for 65+ or blind.

WA.no: No tax on wages. A capital gains excise tax applies to long-term capital gains above a $278,000 standard deduction (2025; $270,000 in 2024). New tiered rates from tax year 2025: 7% on the first $1M of taxable gains and 9.9% above $1M. Real estate and retirement accounts are exempt. The WA Cares long-term-care premium (0.58% of wages) is a payroll deduction, not income tax.

WV.lo: None (some cities charge flat weekly city service/user fees).
WV.no: Rates cut about 4% effective Jan 1, 2025 (W. Va. Code 11-21-4i); another cut is scheduled for 2026. No standard deduction.

WI.no: 2025 Act 15 widened the 4.4% bracket retroactive to Jan 1, 2025 (the Tax Foundation table shows the old $29,370/$39,150 edges). Wisconsin follows the IRC as of Dec 31, 2022. Maximum (sliding-scale) amounts that phase out as income rises. Per the Tax Foundation, the phase-out starts at about $19,549 (single) / $28,209 (MFJ) and reaches zero at about $132,549 / $155,169. Another $250 for each person 65+.

DC.lo: None (DC itself is the local jurisdiction).
DC.no: Brackets are the same for all filing statuses. No 2025 rate change. DC decoupled from the OBBBA increase and keeps $15,000/$30,000 for 2025. It also disallows the federal tips, overtime and senior deductions for 2025.
